text: dsh-cc-switch-bridge 是一个供 DSH 网页客户端使用的模型接入插件。它读取本机 cc-switch 数据库中的 Anthropic 兼容供应商，并为供应商建立模型路由；Codex 配置则交给内置 pi-ai 适配器。设置页面可选择导入的工具分组、查看当前路由并调整顺序，模型选择器随同步结果更新。插件还把供应商模型声明的思考等级映射到 DSH。使用时需在本机配置 cc-switch，并由已保存的供应商凭据和地址连接对应模型服务。

dsh-cc-switch-bridge connects cc-switch providers to DSH. It registers Anthropic-compatible models and passes Codex entries to pi-ai. Users choose groups and reorder routes in settings; the model picker follows synchronization. Local cc-switch entries supply provider addresses and credentials.
想把 cc-switch 里配置的模型放进 DSH 的模型选择器。
能不能在 DSH 设置里挑选要同步的模型来源，并调整它们的显示顺序？
I want my locally saved Anthropic compatible providers to appear as selectable DSH models.
dsh-cc-switch-bridge 的功能「同步模型」：读取本机 cc-switch 配置，为 Anthropic 兼容供应商注册 DSH 路由，并将 Codex 分组交给 pi-ai；插件启动后定时同步。
dsh-cc-switch-bridge 的功能「管理导入分组和顺序」：设置页展示可导入的 cc-switch 分组，可切换选择并拖动已接入路由排序；提交后立即同步，模型选择器按新顺序呈现。
模型请求会发送到 cc-switch 配置中保存的供应商地址，并使用该配置里的凭据；实际目标随本地供应商设置而变。

dsh-cc-switch-bridge README · cc-switch bridge：[中文说明](README.zh.md)

Every Anthropic-compatible provider saved in the local
[cc-switch](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch) app becomes one provider route in DeepSeek
Harness, so its models appear in the model picker and switch like built-in models.

dsh-cc-switch-bridge README · What it reads：`~/.cc-switch/cc-switch.db` (read-only), table `providers`, rows with `app_type` `claude` /
`claude-desktop`. From each row: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`,
the model ids from `meta.stackModels` and the `ANTHROPIC_*MODEL` env keys (`model[1M]` labels keep the
id and give the context window), plus the row name as the group title. Rows are re-read every 60s and
on every model-picker open, so edits made in cc-switch show up without restarting Harness.

dsh-cc-switch-bridge README · What it reads：Rows whose `meta.apiFormat` is anything but `anthropic`, or without a base URL / credential / model,
are skipped and logged. Codex rows are imported through the built-in pi-ai adapter instead (see
Settings page); the other tool groups store their own shapes, see "Why some groups are not imported".

dsh-cc-switch-bridge README · What it registers：One `ctx.llm.registerAdapter()` route per provider (`ccswitch-<first 8 chars of the cc-switch id>`),
speaking Anthropic Messages (`/v1/messages`, SSE or plain JSON) and translating the reply into
Harness stream chunks: text, reasoning/thinking, tool calls, usage, finish reasons. Tool
call/result pairing is repaired before sending, because one unanswered tool call makes the upstream
reject the whole session.

dsh-cc-switch-bridge README · Thinking levels：The levels are not the bridge's own ladder: cc-switch already declares them per model, and the
Harness menu mirrors that declaration, so both apps offer the same choices.

dsh-cc-switch-bridge README · Thinking levels：- `codex` rows carry `modelCatalog.models[].reasoningLevels` (+ `defaultReasoningLevel`), which is
  what cc-switch shows for a Codex provider.
- `pi` rows carry `thinkingLevelMap`, where a `null` value means the level is not offered.
- The row with the same provider name wins; the same model id under another provider only fills in
  what that row does not say.

dsh-cc-switch-bridge README · Thinking levels：`none` in cc-switch is `off` here. Hosts whose endpoint cannot replay a thinking block are excluded in
`replaysWithoutThinking()` in `lib/thinking.js`, and the plugin config `thinking: false` drops every
effort menu.

dsh-cc-switch-bridge README · Settings page：Settings → **cc-switch-bridge** lists the tool groups your cc-switch actually has configured
(Claude Code, Claude Code Desktop, Codex, …) and imports the ones you tick. Changing the selection
re-syncs immediately — no restart — and the model picker follows.

dsh-cc-switch-bridge README · Settings page：| Group                                                          | How it is imported                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Claude Code / Claude Code Desktop / any Anthropic-format group | the bridge's own adapter, one route per provider                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Codex                                                          | handed to the built-in `dsh-llm-pi-ai` adapter: one provider per cc-switch Codex row, `api` taken from the row's `wire_api` (`openai-responses` / `openai-completions`), base URL and model catalog straight from the row |
| pi / o

dsh-cc-switch-bridge README · Settings page：The Codex handoff needs no manual setup: turning it on writes a `codex` entry into the `dsh-llm-pi-ai`
plugin config in the desktop profile patch (`settingsNs: codex`) and stores each row's key in the
credential store under `CCSWITCH_CODEX_<row>`. Turning it off again removes both the routes and the
secrets the bridge wrote.

dsh-cc-switch-bridge README · Settings page：The page itself is a browser half (`client.js`) served by this package and talks to the host over
`/dsh-cc-switch/state` (GET snapshot, POST `{apps, order}` for the selection and its order). The lower
half of the page lists what is actually live, as "bridged" and "handed to pi-ai".

dsh-cc-switch-bridge README · Why some groups are not imported：Not a model problem and not a protocol problem: cc-switch stores one config structure per tool, and the
bridge only parses two of them — `claude` / `claude-desktop` (`env.ANTHROPIC_*`) and `codex` (TOML).
section: Why some groups are not imported

dsh-cc-switch-bridge README · Why some groups are not imported：| Group      | What cc-switch actually stores                                                      | Status                                             |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `pi`       | `baseUrl` / `api` / `models[]` / `thinkingLevelMap` — pi-ai's own provider shape    | fields map almost 1:1, not implemented yet         |
| `openclaw` | `baseUrl` / `api` / `models[]`, also pi-ai-shaped                                   | not implemented yet                                |
| `opencode` | AI SDK `{npm, options, models}` (`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` / `@ai-sdk/anthropic`) | needs a small `npm → api` map, not implemented yet |
| `gemini`   | `{"env":{},"config":{}}` (empty on this machine)                                    | nothing to import                                  |

text:
dsh-cc-switch-bridge README · Status file：`~/.dsh/dsh-cc-switch-bridge.status.json` — written after each successful sync: which routes and models
the host process actually holds. First place to look when a provider is missing from the picker.

dsh-cc-switch-bridge README · Ordering：The bridged and pi-ai rows can be dragged to reorder them; the saved order (`order` in the state
file) is the order the routes are registered in, so it is what the model picker shows. The
DeepSeek account/official groups stay pinned first because the picker does that itself.

dsh-cc-switch-bridge README · After editing this plugin：The profile installs it as a link, but the running host keeps the old module loaded: toggle the
plugin off and on in Settings → Plugins (or restart the app).

dsh-cc-switch-bridge README · Checks：`node tests/smoke.mjs` — SSE decoding, error mapping, tool-call repair, max_tokens clamping, model
labels, ordering, and a read of the real cc-switch database.
`node tests/client-render.mjs` — renders the settings page against a stub React, which catches the
hook-order regression that blanks the page inside the app.
